);

Design a cache replacement policy module that implements the Least Recently Used (LRU) and First-In-First-Out (FIFO) algorithms. The module should take the following inputs:
- `clk`: Clock signal
- `reset`: Asynchronous reset signal
- `cache_in`: Input data to be cached
- `cache_req`: Cache request signal (1 for read, 0 for write)
- `policy`: Control signal to select the replacement policy (0 for LRU, 1 for FIFO)

The output should be:
- `cache_out`: Output data from the cache (for read requests)
- `cache_hit`: Signal indicating whether the data was found in the cache (1 for hit, 0 for miss)
code:
module cache_replacement (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [7:0] cache_in,
    input cache_req,   // 1 for read, 0 for write
    input policy,      // 0 for LRU, 1 for FIFO
    output reg [7:0] cache_out,
    output reg cache_hit
);

    parameter CACHE_SIZE = 4; // 4 entries cache
    reg [7:0] cache_data [0:CACHE_SIZE-1];
    reg [CACHE_SIZE-1:0] valid; // Valid bits for cache entries
    reg [CACHE_SIZE-1:0] lru_counter; // LRU counter
    integer i, lru_index;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < CACHE_SIZE; i = i + 1) begin
                cache_data[i] <= 8'b0;
                valid[i] <= 1'b0;
            end
            cache_hit <= 0;
            lru_counter <= 0;
        end else begin
            cache_hit <= 0; // Default hit signal
            if (cache_req) begin // Read request
                for (i = 0; i < CACHE_SIZE; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (valid[i] && cache_data[i] == cache_in) begin
                        cache_out <= cache_data[i];
                        cache_hit <= 1;
                        if (policy == 0) begin // LRU update
                            lru_counter <= {lru_counter[CACHE_SIZE-2:0], 1'b1};
                            lru_counter[i] <= 0; // Reset the LRU for hit
                        end
                    end
                end
            end else begin // Write request
                if (!cache_hit) begin
                    // Find an empty slot or replace using selected policy
                    if (policy == 0) begin // LRU replacement
                        lru_index = 0;
                        for (i = 1; i < CACHE_SIZE; i = i + 1) begin
                            if (lru_counter[i]) lru_index = i; // Find the LRU
                        end
                    end else begin // FIFO replacement
                        lru_index = (lru_counter[0] == 0) ? 0 : (lru_counter[0] + 1) % CACHE_SIZE;
                    end
                    cache_data[lru_index] <= cache_in;
                    valid[lru_index] <= 1'b1;
                    lru_counter[lru_index] <= 1'b1; // Mark this entry as recently used
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Zero-Crossing Detector. The module detects when an input signal crosses zero and outputs a signal indicating the crossing event. The output should toggle every time the input signal crosses zero from positive to negative or from negative to positive.

module zero_crossing_detector (
    input clk,             // Clock signal
    input rst,             // Reset signal
    input wire signal_in,  // Input signal
    output reg crossing     // Crossing output signal
);

reg previous_signal;

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        crossing <= 0;
        previous_signal <= 0;
    end else begin
        if ((previous_signal == 1 && signal_in == 0) || (previous_signal == 0 && signal_in == 1)) begin
            crossing <= ~crossing; // Toggle crossing output
        end
        previous_signal <= signal_in; // Update previous signal
    end
end

endmodule

description: Implement a simplified version of the ChaCha20 stream cipher's quarter-round function in Verilog. The quarter-round function takes four 32-bit inputs and produces four 32-bit outputs. module quarter_round (
    input wire clk,
    input wire en,
    input wire [31:0] a,
    input wire [31:0] b,
    input wire [31:0] c,
    input wire [31:0] d,
    output reg [31:0] out_a,
    output reg [31:0] out_b,
    output reg [31:0] out_c,
    output reg [31:0] out_d
);

        if (en) begin
            out_a <= a + b; // Add a and b
            out_d <= d ^ out_a; // XOR d with the result of a + b
            out_b <= b + out_d; // Add b and the result of d XOR (a + b)
            out_c <= c ^ out_b; // XOR c with the result of b + (d XOR (a + b))
            out_a <= out_a + out_c; // Add (a + b) and the result of c XOR (b + (d XOR (a + b)))
            out_d <= out_d + out_a; // Final add for d
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit Hamming encoder that takes in 8 bits of data and outputs a 12-bit codeword. The Hamming code should correct single-bit errors. The encoder should include 4 parity bits and will be placed at positions 1, 2, 4, and 8 in the 12-bit output.
code:
module hamming_encoder (
    input [7:0] data,
    output reg [11:0] codeword
);
    always @(*) begin
        codeword[2:0] = data[2:0]; // Data bits
        codeword[3] = data[3]; // Data bit
        codeword[4] = data[4]; // Data bit
        codeword[5] = data[5]; // Data bit
        codeword[6] = data[6]; // Data bit
        codeword[7] = data[7]; // Data bit

        // Calculate parity bits
        codeword[0] = data[0] ^ data[1] ^ data[3] ^ data[4] ^ data[5]; // P1
        codeword[1] = data[0] ^ data[2] ^ data[3] ^ data[6] ^ data[7]; // P2
        codeword[8] = data[1] ^ data[2] ^ data[3] ^ data[6] ^ data[7]; // P4
        codeword[9] = data[4] ^ data[5] ^ data[6] ^ data[7]; // P8
        codeword[10] = 0; // Reserved for further use
        codeword[11] = 0; // Reserved for further use
    end
endmodule

Design a 2-to-1 multiplexer in Verilog. The multiplexer should take two 1-bit inputs (A and B), a 1-bit select input (S), and produce a 1-bit output (Y) based on the select signal. If S is 0, Y should be A; if S is 1, Y should be B.

Design a phase detector that compares two input signals, `signal_a` and `signal_b`. The output should indicate whether `signal_a` is leading, lagging, or the same as `signal_b`. The output should be a 2-bit signal: `00` for equal, `01` for `signal_a` leading, and `10` for `signal_a` lagging.
code:
module phase_detector (
    input wire signal_a,
    input wire signal_b,
    output reg [1:0] phase_out
);

always @(signal_a or signal_b) begin
    if (signal_a == signal_b) begin
        phase_out = 2'b00; // Equal
    end else if (signal_a > signal_b) begin
        phase_out = 2'b01; // signal_a leading
    end else begin
        phase_out = 2'b10; // signal_a lagging
    end
end

endmodule

Design a 3-bit binary to decimal converter. The input is a 3-bit binary number, and the output is a 4-bit decimal value representing the decimal equivalent of the binary input.

Design a 256-bit AES encryption module that takes a 256-bit plaintext and a 256-bit key as inputs and outputs a 256-bit ciphertext. The module should support one round of AES encryption for simplicity.

Design a 1-bit SR flip-flop in Verilog. The SR flip-flop should have inputs S (set), R (reset), and a clock signal CLK.     input wire R,
    input wire CLK,
    output reg Q
);

Design a 4-bit Parallel-In Serial-Out (PISO) shift register. The PISO shift register should have an input for loading data in parallel, a clock input for shifting the data out serially, a load signal to enable parallel loading, and an output for the serial data.     input wire [3:0] data_in,

);

Design a convolutional encoder with a constraint length of 3 and a code rate of 1/2. It takes a stream of input bits and produces two output bits for every input bit. module convolutional_encoder (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input input_bit,
    output reg [1:0] output_bits
);

reg [2:0] shift_reg; // 3-bit shift register

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        shift_reg <= 3'b000;
        output_bits <= 2'b00;
    end else begin
        shift_reg <= {shift_reg[1:0], input_bit}; // Shift left and add new input
        output_bits[0] <= shift_reg[0] ^ shift_reg[1] ^ shift_reg[2]; // Output for G1
        output_bits[1] <= shift_reg[0] ^ shift_reg[2]; // Output for G2
    end
end

endmodule

    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] data_out
);

description: Design a 16-bit CRC generator using a polynomial x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1. The CRC generator should take a 16-bit input data and produce a 16-bit CRC output. The CRC calculation should be performed sequentially, updating the CRC value with each bit of the input data.
code:
module crc_generator (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] crc_out
);
    reg [15:0] crc;
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc <= 16'hFFFF; // Initial value
        end else begin
            crc <= crc ^ data_in; // Start with input data
            for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                if (crc[15] == 1'b1) begin
                    crc <= (crc << 1) ^ 16'hA001; // Polynomial: x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1
                end else begin
                    crc <= crc << 1; // Just shift
                end
            end
            crc_out <= crc; // Update output
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an 8x Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) circuit that takes a reference clock signal as input and outputs an 8 times frequency multiplied clock signal. The PLL should have a feedback topology that allows it to lock to the input frequency and produce the output clock signal.
code:
module pll_8x (
    input wire clk_ref,        // Reference clock input
    input wire reset,          // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out         // Output clock signal (8x)
);
    reg [2:0] counter;         // 3-bit counter to count the reference clock cycles
    
    always @(posedge clk_ref or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            counter <= 3'b000;
            clk_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (counter == 3'b111) begin // Every 8 cycles of clk_ref
                clk_out <= ~clk_out;     // Toggle output clock

    end
endmodule

Create a UART controller that can transmit a byte of data serially. The module should accept an 8-bit data input and a transmit enable signal. When the transmit enable signal is high, the module should start sending the data bit-by-bit, starting from the least significant bit (LSB) to the most significant bit (MSB). Include a clock input to drive the transmission, and a ready signal that indicates when the transmission is complete.
code:
module uart_transmitter(
    input wire clk,
    input wire transmit_en,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg tx,
    output reg ready
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [2:0] bit_index;
    
    localparam WAIT = 4'b0000,
               START = 4'b0001,
               DATA = 4'b0010,
               STOP = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case(state)
            WAIT: begin
                tx <= 1; // idle state
                ready <= 1; // ready to transmit
                if (transmit_en) begin
                    state <= START;
                    bit_index <= 0;
                    ready <= 0; // not ready while transmitting
                end
            end
            
            START: begin
                tx <= 0; // start bit
                state <= DATA;
            end
            
            DATA: begin
                tx <= data_in[bit_index]; // transmit data bit
                if (bit_index < 7) begin
                    bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                end else begin
                    state <= STOP;
                end
            end
            
            STOP: begin
                tx <= 1; // stop bit
                state <= WAIT; // return to wait state
            end
            
            default: state <= WAIT;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Watchdog Timer in Verilog that resets after a specified timeout period unless it receives a 'kick' signal within that period. If the timer times out without a kick, it outputs a reset signal.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset_n,
    input wire kick,
    output reg timeout
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_PERIOD = 8'b11111111; // Example timeout period of 255 clock cycles
    reg [7:0] counter;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            counter <= 8'b0;
            timeout <= 1'b0;
        end else if (kick) begin
            counter <= 8'b0; // Reset counter on kick
            timeout <= 1'b0; // Clear timeout
        end else if (counter == TIMEOUT_PERIOD) begin
            timeout <= 1'b1; // Set timeout when period is reached
        end else begin
            counter <= counter + 1'b1; // Increment counter
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple 2-bit branch predictor using a 2-bit saturating counter. The branch predictor should predict taken or not taken based on the previous outcomes of two branches. The predictor state should be updated based on the actual outcome of the branch. The input will be a 2-bit branch identifier and an actual branch outcome (1 for taken and 0 for not taken). The output will indicate the predicted outcome (1 for taken, 0 for not taken).
code:
module branch_predictor(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [1:0] branch_id,
    input actual_outcome,
    output reg predicted_outcome
);
    reg [1:0] state [3:0]; // State for 4 branches (2-bit saturating counter)

    initial begin
        state[0] = 2'b00; // Strongly Not Taken
        state[1] = 2'b01; // Weakly Not Taken
        state[2] = 2'b10; // Weakly Taken
        state[3] = 2'b11; // Strongly Taken
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            predicted_outcome <= 0;
            // Reset states
            state[0] <= 2'b00;
            state[1] <= 2'b01;
            state[2] <= 2'b10;
            state[3] <= 2'b11;
        end else begin
            predicted_outcome <= (state[branch_id] > 1) ? 1 : 0; // Predict taken if state is 2 or 3
            
            // Update state based on actual outcome
            case (state[branch_id])
                2'b00: if (actual_outcome) state[branch_id] <= 2'b01; // Update to Weakly Not Taken
                2'b01: if (actual_outcome) state[branch_id] <= 2'b10; // Update to Weakly Taken
                2'b10: if (!actual_outcome) state[branch_id] <= 2'b01; // Update to Weakly Not Taken
                        else state[branch_id] <= 2'b11; // Update to Strongly Taken
                2'b11: if (!actual_outcome) state[branch_id] <= 2'b10; // Update to Weakly Taken
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Create a Verilog module for a simple QAM modulator that takes a 4-bit input representing a symbol and outputs two signals: I (in-phase) and Q (quadrature). The mapping should be as follows:
- 0000 -> I = 0, Q = 0
- 0001 -> I = 0, Q = 1
- 0010 -> I = 1, Q = 0
- 0011 -> I = 1, Q = 1
- 0100 -> I = 0, Q = -1
- 0101 -> I = 0, Q = -2
- 0110 -> I = 2, Q = 0

    input clk,

);

    if (rst) begin
        I <= 0;
        Q <= 0;
    end else begin
        case (symbol)
            4'b0000: begin I <= 0; Q <= 0; end
            4'b0001: begin I <= 0; Q <= 1; end
            4'b0010: begin I <= 1; Q <= 0; end
            4'b0011: begin I <= 1; Q <= 1; end

Design a combinational logic circuit in Verilog to evaluate a polynomial of the form: P(x) = a_n*x^n + a_(n-1)*x^(n-1) + ... + a_1*x + a_0, where the coefficients and x are inputs. You need to implement a module that takes the coefficients and x as inputs and outputs the evaluated polynomial result.
code:
module polynomial_evaluator (
    input [3:0] a0, // Coefficient of x^0
    input [3:0] a1, // Coefficient of x^1
    input [3:0] a2, // Coefficient of x^2
    input [3:0] a3, // Coefficient of x^3
    input [3:0] x,   // Input value of x
    output [15:0] P  // Output polynomial result
);
    wire [15:0] x2, x3;
    wire [15:0] term0, term1, term2, term3;

    assign x2 = x * x;           // x^2
    assign x3 = x2 * x;          // x^3
    
    assign term0 = a0;           // a0
    assign term1 = a1 * x;       // a1 * x

    input wire [15:0] R,          // measurement noise covariance

);

            x_new <= 16'b0;
            P <= 16'b0;

The filter should output the estimated position (`x_hat`). The filter equations are as follows:

   P = A * P * A' + Q  
2. Update step:  
   K = P * H' / (H * P * H' + R)  
   x_hat = x_hat + K * (z - H * x_hat)  
   P = (I - K * H) * P

    input reset,
    input [15:0] z,  // noisy measurement
    input [15:0] u,  // control input
    output reg [15:0] x_hat // estimated position
);
    parameter A = 16'h0001; // State transition
    parameter B = 16'h0000; // Control input effect
    parameter H = 16'h0001; // Measurement matrix
    parameter Q = 16'h0001; // Process noise covariance
    parameter R = 16'h0001; // Measurement noise covariance

    reg [15:0] P; // estimation error covariance
    reg [15:0] K; // Kalman gain
    reg [15:0] z_pred; // predicted measurement

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x_hat <= 16'b0;
            P <= 16'h0001; // Initial estimation error covariance
        end else begin
            // Prediction step
            x_hat <= A * x_hat + B * u; // Update state estimate
            P <= A * P * A + Q; // Update estimation error covariance

            // Update step
            z_pred <= H * x_hat; // Predicted measurement
            K <= P * H / (H * P * H + R); // Calculate Kalman gain

    output reg done

        data[2] = 4'b0011; next[2] = 3'b011; // Node 2

            current <= next[current]; // Move to the next node

    input clk,
    input [15:0] x0, // First input sample (real, imaginary)
    input [15:0] x1, // Second input sample (real, imaginary)
    input [15:0] x2, // Third input sample (real, imaginary)
    input [15:0] x3, // Fourth input sample (real, imaginary)
    output reg [15:0] y0, // Output sample 0
    output reg [15:0] y1, // Output sample 1
    output reg [15:0] y2, // Output sample 2
    output reg [15:0] y3  // Output sample 3
);
    reg [15:0] stage0 [0:3]; // Internal storage for stage 0 results
    reg [15:0] stage1 [0:3]; // Internal storage for stage 1 results
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // Stage 0: Calculate the basic butterflies
        stage0[0] <= x0 + x1; // Y0 = X0 + X1
        stage0[1] <= x0 - x1; // Y1 = X0 - X1
        stage0[2] <= x2 + x3; // Y2 = X2 + X3
        stage0[3] <= x2 - x3; // Y3 = X2 - X3
        
        // Stage 1: Calculate the final butterflies
        y0 <= stage0[0] + stage0[2]; // Y0 = Y0 + Y2
        y1 <= stage0[1] + (stage0[3] * 16'h0_0000); // Y1 = Y1 + j*Y3
        y2 <= stage0[0] - stage0[2]; // Y2 = Y0 - Y2
        y3 <= stage0[1] - (stage0[3] * 16'h0_0000); // Y3 = Y1 - j*Y3
    end
endmodule

module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input req1,
    input req2,
    input [31:0] src_addr1,
    input [31:0] src_addr2,
    input [31:0] dest_addr1,
    input [31:0] dest_addr2,
    output reg active1,
    output reg active2,
    output reg [31:0] data1,
    output reg [31:0] data2,
    output reg transfer_done
);
    reg [3:0] state; // State for transfer
    parameter IDLE = 0, TRANSFER1 = 1, TRANSFER2 = 2, DONE = 3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            active1 <= 0;
            active2 <= 0;
            transfer_done <= 0;
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (req1) begin
                        active1 <= 1;
                        data1 <= src_addr1; // Simulate data transfer
                        state <= TRANSFER1;
                    end else if (req2) begin
                        active2 <= 1;
                        data2 <= src_addr2; // Simulate data transfer
                        state <= TRANSFER2;
                    end
                end
                TRANSFER1: begin
                    // Simulate transfer time
                    if (active1) begin
                        data1 <= data1 + 1; // Increment data as a simple transfer simulation
                        state <= DONE;
                    end
                end
                TRANSFER2: begin
                    if (active2) begin
                        data2 <= data2 + 1; // Increment data as a simple transfer simulation
                        state <= DONE;
                    end
                end
                DONE: begin

    end
endmodule

description: Design a noise suppression circuit that filters unwanted glitches in a digital signal. The circuit should take a noisy signal as input and output a clean signal. If a noisy signal is detected for less than a preset threshold, the output should retain the last known stable value. The circuit should allow for configuration of the threshold for noise detection.

module noise_suppression (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire noisy_signal,
    input wire threshold,
    output reg clean_signal
);
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg last_stable_value;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            count <= 0;
            clean_signal <= 0;
            last_stable_value <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (noisy_signal == clean_signal) begin
                count <= 0; // Reset count if signal is stable
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1; // Increment count on noise
                if (count >= threshold) begin
                    clean_signal <= noisy_signal; // Update clean signal if threshold is reached
                    last_stable_value <= clean_signal;
                end else begin
                    clean_signal <= last_stable_value; // Maintain last stable value

endmodule

Create a simple 2-bit branch predictor that predicts whether the next branch will be taken or not based on the current branch outcome. The predictor will use a 1-bit saturating counter for each branch to make the prediction. The state transitions are as follows:
- If the prediction is "taken" and the actual outcome is "taken," stay in the same state (strongly taken).
- If the prediction is "taken" and the actual outcome is "not taken," move to "weakly taken."
- If the prediction is "not taken" and the actual outcome is "not taken," stay in the same state (strongly not taken).
- If the prediction is "not taken" and the actual outcome is "taken," move to "weakly not taken."
The 2-bit counter states can be represented as:
00 - strongly not taken
01 - weakly not taken
10 - weakly taken
11 - strongly taken
code:
module branch_predictor(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire branch_outcome, // 0 for not taken, 1 for taken
    output reg prediction // 0 for not taken, 1 for taken
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 2-bit state
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Initial state (strongly not taken)
            prediction <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // strongly not taken
                    prediction <= 0;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b01; // move to weakly not taken
                end
                2'b01: begin // weakly not taken
                    prediction <= 0;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // move to weakly taken
                    else state <= 2'b00; // stay in strongly not taken
                end
                2'b10: begin // weakly taken
                    prediction <= 1;
                    if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b11; // move to strongly taken
                    else state <= 2'b01; // move to weakly not taken
                end
                2'b11: begin // strongly taken
                    prediction <= 1;
                    if (!branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // move to weakly taken
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple RRT (Rapidly-exploring Random Tree) algorithm for pathfinding in a 2D space. The module should take the current position and a target position as inputs, and at each clock cycle, it should attempt to extend the tree towards the target position by generating a random point within a defined range, and then updating the current position towards that point. The module should have an output that indicates the new position after each update.

Design an 8-channel DMA controller that can select one of the 8 channels based on a 3-bit channel select input. The controller should have an enable signal that, when asserted, starts the data transfer from the selected channel. The output should indicate which channel is currently active. The controller should also reset to a known state when the reset signal is asserted.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [2:0] channel_select,
    output reg [7:0] active_channel
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        active_channel <= 8'b00000000;
    end else if (enable) begin
        active_channel <= 8'b00000000; // Clear previous channel
        active_channel[channel_select] <= 1'b1; // Set active channel
    end
end

endmodule

Design a simple finite state machine (FSM) that implements a Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal mechanism on a binary tree. The FSM should take an input signal indicating the current node and output the next node in the BFS order. The states represent the nodes being traversed, and the output should reflect the next node to visit.
code:
module bfs_fsm(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] current_node,
    output reg [3:0] next_node
);
    reg [3:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 4'b0000; // Initial state
            next_node <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                4'b0000: begin // Node 0
                    next_node <= 4'b0001; // Next node 1
                    state <= 4'b0001;
                end
                4'b0001: begin // Node 1
                    next_node <= 4'b0010; // Next node 2
                    state <= 4'b0010;
                end
                4'b0010: begin // Node 2
                    next_node <= 4'b0011; // Next node 3
                    state <= 4'b0011;
                end
                4'b0011: begin // Node 3
                    next_node <= 4'b0100; // Next node 4
                    state <= 4'b0100;
                end
                4'b0100: begin // Node 4
                    next_node <= 4'b0000; // Loop back to start
                    state <= 4'b0000;
                end
                default: begin
                    next_node <= 4'b0000;
                    state <= 4'b0000;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Parallel-In Serial-Out (PISO) shift register. The PISO shift register should have an input data width of 5 bits and a clock input. It should have a load enable signal to load the parallel data when high, and a serial output signal that shifts out each bit on the clock pulse when the load enable is low.
code:
module piso_shift_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [4:0] parallel_data,
    output reg serial_out
);

    reg [4:0] shift_reg;
    integer bit_count;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= parallel_data; // Load parallel data
            bit_count <= 4; // Set to 4 (least significant bit first)
        end else if (bit_count >= 0) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[bit_count]; // Output the current bit
            bit_count <= bit_count - 1; // Move to the next bit
        end
    end

endmodule

Design a D-latch that captures the input data (D) on the rising edge of the clock (CLK) and holds the output (Q) until the next rising edge. The D-latch should have an active-low enable signal (EN) that allows the latch to update its output only when EN is low. If EN is high, the output Q should retain its previous value.
code:
module D_latch (
    input wire D,
    input wire CLK,
    input wire EN,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge CLK or negedge EN) begin
        if (!EN) begin
            Q <= D;
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a fixed-priority arbiter in Verilog that takes multiple request signals and generates a single grant signal based on the fixed priority of the requests. The arbiter should have 4 request inputs (req0, req1, req2, req3), and a single grant output (grant) that indicates which request is granted based on priority (req0 has the highest priority and req3 has the lowest). The arbiter should also have a clock input for synchronization and a reset input to clear the state.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire req0,
    input wire req1,
    input wire req2,
    input wire req3,
    output reg [1:0] grant
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        grant <= 2'b00; // No grant
    end else begin
        if (req0) grant <= 2'b00; // Grant req0
        else if (req1) grant <= 2'b01; // Grant req1
        else if (req2) grant <= 2'b10; // Grant req2
        else if (req3) grant <= 2'b11; // Grant req3
        else grant <= 2'b00; // No grant
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a linear voltage regulator in Verilog that takes a varying input voltage and provides a stable output voltage. The regulator should compare the input voltage with a reference voltage and adjust the output accordingly. The output should be enabled only if the input voltage is above the reference voltage; otherwise, the output should be zero.
code:
module linear_voltage_regulator(

);

description: Design a fixed-priority arbiter in Verilog. The arbiter has three request inputs (req[2:0]) and one grant output (grant). The arbiter should grant access based on fixed priority: req[2] > req[1] > req[0]. If multiple requests are made simultaneously, the request with the highest priority should be granted. The output grant should be a one-hot encoded signal indicating which request is being granted.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [2:0] req,
    output reg [2:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            grant <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            grant <= 3'b000; // Reset grant
            if (req[2]) begin
                grant[2] <= 1'b1; // Grant to req[2]
            end else if (req[1]) begin
                grant[1] <= 1'b1; // Grant to req[1]
            end else if (req[0]) begin
                grant[0] <= 1'b1; // Grant to req[0]
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit SRAM cell. The SRAM cell should have the following inputs: 8-bit data input (data_in), a write enable signal (we), and a clock signal (clk). The output should be an 8-bit data output (data_out). When write enable is high, on the rising edge of the clock, the data input should be written to the SRAM cell. When write enable is low, the data output should reflect the stored value in the SRAM cell.
code:
module sram_cell (
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire we,
    input wire clk,
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    reg [7:0] storage;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (we) begin
            storage <= data_in; // Write data to SRAM
        end
        data_out <= storage; // Output stored data
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 5-bit ring counter in Verilog. The counter should have a reset input that initializes the counter to '00001'. The counter should shift the '1' bit to the left on every clock cycle. When the counter reaches the end, it should wrap around to the beginning. The output of the counter should be a 5-bit vector.
code:
module ring_counter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    output reg [4:0] count
);
    
    initial begin
        count = 5'b00001; // Initialize the counter
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            count <= 5'b00001; // Reset to '00001'
        end else begin
            count <= {count[3:0], count[4]}; // Shift left
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a combinational logic circuit for Huffman encoding. The circuit should take a 4-bit binary input representing a character and output a 3-bit binary code corresponding to its Huffman encoding. The mapping is as follows:
- 0000 -> 00
- 0001 -> 01
- 0010 -> 10
- 0011 -> 110
- 0100 -> 111

    input [3:0] char_input,
    output reg [2:0] huffman_code
);

        default: huffman_code = 3'b111;  // not found
    endcase
end

endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm on a predefined graph represented as an adjacency matrix. The module should take a start vertex as input and output a sequence of visited vertices in the order they were visited during the DFS traversal.
code:
module DFS (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [2:0] start_vertex,
    output reg [2:0] visited_vertex,
    output reg done
);
    reg [7:0] stack [0:7]; // Stack to hold vertices (max 8 vertices)
    reg [2:0] top; // Stack pointer
    reg [7:0] visited; // Visited vertices
    reg [2:0] current_vertex; // Current vertex being processed

    initial begin
        top = 0;
        visited = 0;
        done = 0;
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            top <= 0;
            visited <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            visited_vertex <= 0;
        end else if (!done) begin
            if (top == 0) begin
                stack[top] <= start_vertex;
                top <= top + 1;
            end else begin
                current_vertex = stack[top - 1];
                top <= top - 1; // Pop the stack
                if ((visited & (1 << current_vertex)) == 0) begin
                    visited = visited | (1 << current_vertex);
                    visited_vertex <= current_vertex;
                    // Push adjacent vertices (for simplicity, let's assume a fixed adjacency)
                    if (current_vertex == 0) begin
                        stack[top] <= 1; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 0
                        stack[top] <= 2; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 0
                    end else if (current_vertex == 1) begin
                        stack[top] <= 3; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 1
                    end else if (current_vertex == 2) begin
                        stack[top] <= 4; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 2
                    end else if (current_vertex == 3) begin
                        stack[top] <= 5; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 3
                    end else if (current_vertex == 4) begin
                        stack[top] <= 6; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 4
                    end else if (current_vertex == 5) begin
                        stack[top] <= 7; top <= top + 1; // Adjacent to 5
                    end
                end
            end
            if (top == 0) begin
                done <= 1; // Finished DFS
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit divider that takes a 4-bit numerator and a 4-bit denominator and produces a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder. The circuit should handle division by zero by outputting a defined error value for both quotient and remainder when the denominator is zero.
code:
module divider_4bit (
    input [3:0] numerator,
    input [3:0] denominator,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder
);
    always @(*) begin
        if (denominator == 4'b0000) begin
            quotient = 4'b1111; // Error code for division by zero
            remainder = 4'b1111; // Error code for division by zero
        end else begin
            quotient = numerator / denominator;
            remainder = numerator % denominator;
        end
    end
endmodule
